actions.action: Slide plant out of pot and inspect roots
Cut off any rotted roots with clean scissors
If rot is bad, repot in fresh chunky mix of potting soil, perlite and bark
Check that inner pot has drainage holes
Water thoroughly when top 2-3 inches of soil are dry and let drain
Move plant to bright indirect light
Prune brown shriveled stem sections and dead stubs
Fertilize lightly once new growth appears
Tie plant to pole more securely with soft ties
If roots mostly rotted, propagate a node cutting in water or sphagnum moss
Report watering frequency, light and root condition for further diagnosis

reason: The answer leads with watering/root rot and only secondarily notes low light and loose pole attachment, so the diagnosis is partial. Repotting (conditional on rot), more light and tying to the pole are present but buried, with no guidance on positioning nodes against the pole, so the advice is partial. Nothing recommended is likely to harm the plant.
